title: The Client's Message
notes: Detective-cast (Kogoro, Ran, Conan, Megure, Takagi) omitted by convention, except where their actions cause a plot-relevant node/edge (e.g. Conan finding the hidden lamp is folded into the lamp's discovery rather than an event node). Kogoro was the investigator Kaoru Sasamori secretly hired to check whether Tsuge was cheating on her -- the episode title refers to Tsuge's own posthumous 'message' (the shadow-art sculpture), not that hiring. No `event` nodes: actions are direct typed edges. Correction vs. the old cases/ep689 file: the old file's culprit id (Ishikura) is correct, but its single object node 'Missing sculpture weapon' conflates two separate props -- the actual murder weapon was a hammer (left at the scene, prints wiped), and the object Ishikura actually removed and hid afterward was a lamp needed to cast the sculpture's incriminating shadow, not a weapon. That distinction is the load-bearing clue in the episode (the wet driver's seat / physique-under-the-workbench reasoning is about recovering the lamp, not a weapon), so it is modeled here as two separate objects. case_type: murder.

attrs.hired_investigator: secretly hired Kogoro Mouri to check if boyfriend Tsuge was cheating, shortly before her death

attrs.name_meaning: artist name 'Hikari Tsuge' is an anagram of real name 'Ritsu Hikage'; hikari/kage = light/shadow
attrs.backstory_action: spent 3 months secretly identifying Kaoru's killer, encoding the answer into a shadow-art sculpture

attrs.belief: believed Tsuge would marry her once Kaoru was out of the way

attrs.significance: where Kaoru fell to her death
hidden from view of cars driving up the hill

attrs.trick: shapeless from most angles; a lamp at the right angle casts a ballerina-shaped shadow identifying the killer

attrs.staging_flaw: fingerprints wiped off; left at the scene, unlike the lamp

attrs.purpose: needed to illuminate the sculpture and cast the incriminating ballerina shadow
attrs.removed_because: killer feared the shadow would be seen

clues.desc: Tsuge's real name 'Ritsu Hikage' anagrams to his artist name, and the sculpture's title 'Demurrer' anagrams to 'Murderer' -- the victim encoded the killer's identity in the same wordplay that was his own signature.
Reaching the lamp meant crawling under the workbench (blood blocked stepping over the body); Sasamori's and Noguchi's builds don't fit underneath, but ballerina Ishikura's does.
Ishikura arrived without an umbrella and soaking wet, but her car's driver's seat was also drenched -- proving she'd already been out in the rain (hiding the lamp) before 'arriving'.

edges.detail: Tsuge once said, out of frustration, he'd marry her if Kaoru were gone; Ishikura took it as a literal promise
accuses Tsuge of pushing Kaoru down the stairs, at her funeral

edges.motive_type: financial: Tsuge's productivity dropped after dating Kaoru, threatening Noguchi's client contracts; she paid Kaoru ¥1,000,000 to break up (red herring)
jealousy: wanted Tsuge to herself, saw Kaoru as an obstacle to marriage
self-preservation: to silence Tsuge before he revealed she killed Kaoru
revenge: mistakenly believed Tsuge pushed his sister down the stairs (red herring)

edges.method: struck on the back of the head with a hammer
